output.review_comment:
Most of the fix is right. Rule 1 now keeps words with internal uppercase (iPhone, NASA) exactly as written. Rule 2 now capitalizes a small word at the end of the title. And `capitalize()` is only used on words with no internal uppercase, so it doesn't lowercase anything it shouldn't.

The problem is the `is_after_colon` branch, which capitalizes a small word that follows a colon. The docstring says a small word is capitalized only if it is the first or last word of the text, and the teammate said the docstring is the source of truth. The PR description admits this branch was added "only so that test_subtitle_after_colon passes" and that it "conflicts with the docstring." That is code written to satisfy one test, and it knowingly breaks the spec. It also quietly changes the output of `title_case`, which the article pipeline uses, for every title with a subtitle.

Please:
1. Remove the after-colon logic so the code does exactly what the docstring says.
2. Leave test_subtitle_after_colon failing and flag it. Under the docstring the correct output is "Notes From the Field: a Year of Remote Work", so the test's expected value doesn't match the spec.
3. Ask the team which one is intended. If subtitles should be capitalized after a colon, update the docstring and README first, then add the code.

Neither the tests nor the docstring should be changed quietly to make the suite pass.
